title: Cisco CCST IT Support (100-140) Study Guide
description: The Cisco Certified Support Technician (CCST) IT Support is Cisco's direct answer to CompTIA A+ — one $125 exam instead of two ~$274 vouchers, covering real help-desk work: tickets and SLAs, hardware, Windows/macOS/mobile troubleshooting, connectivity, security threats, and remote-support tools. The catch is recognition: A+ has decades of HR mindshare; this is the newcomer.
audience: Students whose schools offer it, career changers for whom A+'s ~$550 exam cost is a genuine barrier, and anyone who wants a legitimate, current help-desk credential at the lowest possible price. English-only exam — worth knowing for non-native speakers who'd prefer A+'s language options.
why_get_it: The math and the material. One exam at $125 versus A+'s two exams at ~$274 each is a real difference when you're funding your own start. And the content is genuinely job-relevant — more current than A+ in spots: ticket queues, SLAs and KPIs, remote-support tooling, even using AI as a support tool, which reflects what 2026 help desks actually look like. The honest catch: almost no job filter searches for CCST IT Support yet. A+ appears in a huge share of support listings; this appears in almost none. Recognition is growing through the high-school pipeline and it carries ACE college-credit recommendation, but a hiring manager who hasn't heard of it won't weight it like A+. A CCST plus a good homelab story beats no cert — it doesn't yet beat A+.
when_to_get_it: When budget decides: if ~$550 in A+ vouchers is the barrier between you and a first credential, CCST IT Support at $125 is the legitimate alternative — take it, apply anyway, and let the interview carry you. When your school offers it: free-to-you plus ACE credit is an easy yes. When you're job hunting within six months in a market that lists A+ by name: save toward A+ instead, or do the Google IT Support Certificate first and use its 30% A+ discount. Note this cert bridges sideways (to CCST Networking or Cybersecurity), not upward — unlike CCST Networking, there's no natural Cisco follow-on above it.
salary_note: Maps directly to help desk technician and IT support specialist roles at roughly $38–52K U.S. entry — the same seats A+ feeds, because it competes head-on with A+ for exactly these jobs. The cert doesn't set the pay; availability, communication, and any customer-service history move entry offers more than the badge choice does.
exam_format: 40–50 questions (multiple choice plus performance-based items), via Certiport or Pearson VUE (test center or OnVUE online). English only. Unlimited retakes, instant results. Passing score not published.
recertification_note: Same 2025 policy as all CCSTs: earned on/after July 15, 2025 = 5-year validity (exam-only renewal); earned before = lifetime. CE credits don't apply.

items: Ticketing systems, SLAs, KPIs — the metrics help desks live by
Professional communication and active listening (yes, it's graded)
Documentation habits that make tier-2 love you
Using AI assistants as a support tool — new, and genuinely current
Diagnosing hardware issues: power, storage, memory, peripherals
Basic networking from the support seat: Wi-Fi, DNS, DHCP symptoms
When it's the cable (it's often the cable)
Windows, macOS, and mobile troubleshooting workflows
Application issues: installs, updates, crashes, profiles
Common threats a help desk sees first: phishing, malware symptoms
Prevention basics and when to sound the alarm
Account security: resets, MFA, lockouts done right

study_steps.title: Work the free official path
study_steps.description: NetAcad's IT Support Specialist path (~30 hours, free) is the official prep. Supplement with the free mini-courses — Computer Hardware Basics (6h), Operating Systems Basics (12h), IT Customer Support Basics (4h) — which map directly onto the blueprint domains.

study_steps.title: Read the actual blueprint PDF
study_steps.description: The 100-140 blueprint is the newest and least-covered CCST — third-party prep is thin, so the official topic list matters more here than usual. Six domains, no published weights. Note the soft-skills content: communication is genuinely tested.

study_steps.title: Build the homelab story
study_steps.description: This cert plus a demonstrable story beats the cert alone: wipe and rebuild an old PC, set up remote-desktop access, document three 'tickets' you solved at home in write-up form. That's your interview material — the exam's troubleshooting scenarios get easier too.

study_steps.title: Demo the interface, then book
study_steps.description: Certiport's free Test Drive first, then book via Certiport (schools) or Pearson VUE (individuals — test center or online from home). Remember it's English-only, unlike the other two CCSTs.

study_steps.title: Apply immediately — don't wait for more certs
study_steps.description: Help desk is the one genuinely entry-level IT tier. CCST + homelab story + any customer-service history is an application-ready package. Apply while momentum is high; add A+ later if your market demands it.

study_steps.title: Branch deliberately from here
study_steps.description: CCST IT Support has no Cisco follow-on above it — the bridges run sideways: CCST Networking → CCNA if infrastructure pulls you, CCST Cybersecurity → Security+ if defense does. Six months of real tickets will tell you which. Our Help Desk Technician path maps both exits.

faq.question: CCST IT Support or CompTIA A+ — the honest answer?
faq.answer: A+ if your job market lists it and you can afford ~$548 for both exams — three decades of HR mindshare is worth real money. CCST IT Support if budget is the barrier, your school offers it, or you want current, job-relevant material for $125 and are willing to let the interview do more work. Middle path many take: Google IT Support Certificate first (~$150), then its 30% A+ discount, then both on the resume.

faq.question: Do employers recognize CCST IT Support?
faq.answer: Honestly, mostly not yet. It's the newest CCST (launched 2024), appears in very few job filters, and is English-only. Recognition is growing through the high-school CTE pipeline and it carries ACE college-credit recommendation — but today its value is proof of readiness plus the Cisco brand, not keyword matches. Pair it with a homelab story and apply anyway; help desk hiring forgives thin credentials more than any other IT tier.

faq.question: What makes it different from A+ in content?
faq.answer: It's leaner (one 50-minute exam vs two 90-minute ones) and more current in spots — ticketing/SLA/KPI workflows, remote-support tooling, and AI-assisted troubleshooting are first-class topics, which A+ covers lightly or not at all. A+ goes deeper on hardware minutiae and has broader OS coverage. For the actual day-one job, the content gap is smaller than the recognition gap.

faq.question: What comes after it?
faq.answer: Sideways, then up: CCST IT Support has no direct Cisco cert above it. The natural moves are CCST Networking → CCNA (infrastructure lane) or CCST Cybersecurity → Security+ (security lane), decided by which tickets you enjoy most after a few months in the seat.

faq.question: Does it expire?
faq.answer: Earned before July 15, 2025: lifetime. On or after: 5 years, exam-only renewal (any current CCST or higher Cisco exam). CE credits don't apply at this tier.
